grh_e13d3bef4dd6bfb3a8bc.title: The Desert Song
paragraphs: Pierre, the French governor's seemingly idle son, secretly leads oppressed desert tribes as the masked Red Shadow. Margot is drawn both to Pierre and to the daring outlaw without knowing they are the same man, while Pierre's own father is determined to destroy the Red Shadow. Pierre refuses a fight that would betray the people he protects and is cast into the desert, but his identity is eventually uncovered. He stages the Red Shadow's disappearance, wins his father's respect, and reunites with Margot, who discovers that the two men she loved were one and the same.

Other credited names include Jean Holloway as radio adaptor, Gordon MacRae as host, and Marvin Miller as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 45 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.f7185f50dd01455d|Association of American Railroads]].
This version dramatizes [[work|work.rr.d66561cde1e924d1|The Desert Song]]. Jean Holloway adapted it for radio.

grh_e17c4d808340b356f82f.title: Still Time to Die
paragraphs: A dramatization of correspondent Jack Belden's Still Time to Die rejects sanitized or triumphalist descriptions of modern war. Recovering from wounds, Belden recalls the hunger, bombing, fear and misery he witnessed from Malta to the battlefields of Europe and contrasts those realities with confident commentary heard far from combat. Returning to the United States, he warns that prejudice, reaction and authoritarian thinking can exist at home as well as abroad, and concludes that military victory must be joined to a continuing fight for genuine democratic freedom.

The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes.
